newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu asks for a meeting with Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu asks for a meeting with Arafat.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has asked for a meeting with Yasser Arafat to try to revive peace talks but the Palestinian president was non-committal, a PLO official said on Monday.

He said Netanyahu aide Asaad al-Asaad conveyed the message to Arafat when the Israeli official accompanied a 17-member delegation from the Israeli-Arab Druze sect which met the Palestinian leader in the West Bank town of Ramallah on Monday.
"Arafat did not commit himself, responding by asking Netanyahu to implement (peace) agreements," the PLO official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
A Netanyahu spokesman confirmed Asaad conveyed a message from the Israeli leader to Arafat but declined to give any details.
Israeli-PLO peace talks have been frozen since Netanyahu began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.

Arafat also wants Netanyahu to honour interim self-rule deals requiring Israel to redeploy its troops from rural areas in the West Bank and start talks on a permanent peace deal that would also deal with the future of East Jerusalem, which Israel claims as part of its capital.
Separate efforts by the United States and Egypt to revive the peace talks have failed to produce any results.
